sections.h2: Where to bring a signed deed
sections.html:
The Jackson County Register of Deeds is at 120 W Michigan Ave, 12th Floor, Jackson, MI 49201. The counter opens 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., Monday through Friday, and stays open over lunch. Call 517-788-4350 with questions. County holidays are days off.

Most sellers never make the trip. Your closing agent normally files the deed and pays the fees. Transfer tax is still yours, and it shows as a deduction from your proceeds, so it pays to understand how the counter treats it.

One office handles the whole county, whether the parcel is in the city of Jackson or in a village such as Brooklyn, Concord, Grass Lake, Hanover, Parma, Springport or Cement City. The county has 159,552 residents and 69,801 housing units, and 75.0 percent of occupied homes are owner occupied.

The recording charge is a flat $30 for one document of any length. It has been in place since October 1, 2016, and $4 of it goes toward survey monument upkeep. The authority is MCL 600.2567.

Smaller charges that may apply:

  • $3 per extra instrument when one paper assigns or discharges several.
  • Page copies at $1, and $5 for a certified document.
  • Name searches at 50 cents per year searched, $5 at the least.
  • Tax lien name searches, state or federal, at $3 each.

Payment is accepted by cash, check or card. Make checks payable to the Register of Deeds, and transfer tax can go on that same check.

A sale triggers two taxes. The county rate is 55 cents and the state rate $3.75, each applied per $500 of price, with any leftover part of $500 billed as a whole step. The seller is the taxpayer under MCL 207.523, and the county's share is set by MCL 207.504.

Put the full price on the deed. To leave the price off the document, file a valuation affidavit and say so on the deed. The affidavit has no filing fee. An exemption claim also goes on the deed itself.

sections.h2: Deeds that owe no transfer tax
sections.html:
Some transfers are exempt, though the county and state lists differ. Both taxes skip a deed given as security, a transfer under $100, and a deed between spouses that creates or ends a tenancy by the entireties. The state tax also skips a deed from a parent or grandparent to a child, stepchild, grandchild or step-grandchild, plus deeds made through a foreclosure or in lieu of one. See MCL 207.526.

The county list in MCL 207.505 is shorter. So a gift deed to a daughter or son may owe no state tax but still owe county tax. Call the register of deeds and describe the exact deed before anyone signs.

Tax paid on a deed that turns out to be exempt can be reclaimed by asking the state treasury department for a refund.

Any deed with warranty language needs one, and so do land contracts and assignments of them that include a warranty clause. The county treasurer first certifies the tax history that MCL 211.135 covers, five years back from the date of the deed. A quitclaim deed with no warranties is excepted.

The certificate costs $5 in Jackson County. It needs its own check payable to the Jackson County Treasurer, submitted along with the deed.

When taxes are owed on the house, request the payoff amount early. Closing pays it out of your sale proceeds.

sections.h2: Why a deed gets sent back
sections.html:
Paper that breaks MCL 565.201 comes back unrecorded. The usual culprits are layout slips and missing names:

  • Sheets outside the legal size range, faint ink, or type below 10 point.
  • A top band on page one that is under 2.5 inches.
  • A first printed line that fails to say which single event is being recorded.
  • No printed name beneath a signature, a notary name on a different page from the notary's signature, or no grantee address.
  • Missing drafter name and business address.
  • Unredacted social security numbers.

Photocopies are refused, because only original signatures qualify. Court papers need the court seal, and a death certificate needs the clerk's seal. The office cannot write your deed or sell forms. An attorney or title agent can.

sections.h2: Step by step when you record the deed yourself
sections.html:
Closings rarely need this, but anyone filing alone can follow a short path. First, confirm the deed type and whether it carries warranty language, since that decides whether a treasurer's certificate is needed. Second, compare the layout to the list above before printing. Third, sign before a notary, in original ink.

Then take the deed, the $30 fee, any transfer tax and the separate $5 treasurer check to 120 W Michigan Ave. Ask the counter if your exemption is on the correct list. Bring a phone or pen for notes, and ask the clerk to confirm the recording date before you leave. If something is wrong, staff return the paper and you fix it and file again, so allow a little time before a closing date.

Hold on to a copy of the recorded deed, along with your receipt. A later buyer or title agent will want it first.

Owners are the bulk of the market. Median monthly owner costs run $1,377 with a mortgage and $557 without, and median rent is $985. The middle home value is $193,700, and 21.5 percent of residents are 65 or older.

Because more than one resident in five is past 65, sales following a death or a move into care are common. A tidy deed history speeds those along.

Land near the Grand River in the city of Jackson, or the north branch of the Kalamazoo River in Hanover Township, may carry easements in its recorded history. Request a records search if yours might.

The online grantor and grantee name search spans deeds, mortgages and miscellaneous papers. High volume copy buyers may request an escrow account. You can also bring your parcel's legal description to the counter, and staff will help you start a records search. Questions about easements or lake rights are often answered by the title insurance policy you received when you bought.

Owners can enroll in a free alert that reports any filing made under their name. It is a no cost way to spot a forged deed.

What to gather for a buyer

When a buyer asks a title question, assemble your recorded deed, your loan payoff letter and any lien notices. That bundle covers most requests. A cash buyer has no lender demanding extra title paperwork, so these pieces are often enough.

faqs.q: Does the recording fee go up with extra pages?
faqs.a: No. A long deed costs the same $30 as a short one. The only add on is $3 for each extra instrument a single paper assigns or discharges.

faqs.q: Who owes transfer tax on a Jackson County sale?
faqs.a: The seller does. The county takes 55 cents and the state $3.75 on each $500 of price, unless the deed states a valid exemption.

faqs.q: Will the office record a copy of my deed?
faqs.a: No. Only the original signed paper is taken. Court orders carry the court seal, and death certificates carry the clerk's seal.

faqs.q: Is a tax certificate needed for a quitclaim deed?
faqs.a: Usually no, since the statute exempts quitclaim deeds that carry no warranty covenants. Warranty deeds and land contracts are the ones that need it.

faqs.q: When can I visit the Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: Come Monday to Friday between 8 and 4, noon hour included. Legal holidays are days off, so call 517-788-4350 first.
